title: Gandhi and Sarojini Naidu: The High Cost of Poverty!
summary: Sarojini Naidu famously teased the Mahatma: 'If only you knew, Bapu, how much money it costs us to keep you in poverty!'
keywords: Gandhi and Sarojini Naidu: The High Cost of Poverty!
full_text:
While life in Mahatma Gandhi's ashrams was governed by strict vows of truth, simplicity, and service, it was never dour or humorless.

Among the inner circle, no one teased the Mahatma with greater affection and irreverence than the celebrated poet and freedom fighter Sarojini Naidu. She famously nicknamed Gandhi 'Mickey Mouse' because of his prominent ears and toothless grin—a moniker the Mahatma enjoyed immensely.

Gandhi insisted on traveling by third-class rail and subsisting entirely on goat's milk, raw vegetables, and unpolished grain.

However, ensuring that a herd of healthy goats was stationed wherever the Mahatma traveled, chartering special third-class train compartments to manage overwhelming crowds, and securing mud cottages for his entourage required frantic logistical efforts funded by industrialists like G. D. Birla and Jamnalal Bajaj!

One afternoon at Wardha Ashram, Sarojini Naidu watched the whirlwind of volunteers bustling about to prepare the Mahatma's goat milk and spinning wheel.

Sighing dramatically, she looked at Gandhi and proclaimed with mock despair:
**"If only you knew, Bapu, how much money it costs us to keep you in poverty!"**

The entire room dissolved into helpless laughter.

Gandhi adjusted his spectacles, looked at Sarojini with sparkling eyes, and retorted:
"My dear Sarojini! Does my poverty burden you so heavily? If that is the case, perhaps I should pack my spinning wheel and come live in your home as a permanent house guest!"

Sarojini threw up her hands in comic horror:
"Heaven forbid, Bapu! If you move into my house, my kitchen will be invaded by goats and neem juice concoctions! Stay right here in your ashram; we will gladly pay the price of keeping you poor!"

Their banter illustrates the radiant warmth that sustained the architects of Indian independence through decades of imprisonment and struggle.
moral: Warmth, laughter, and self-effacing humor are essential shields against the bitterness of long political struggles.
